column1: # The behaviours of the resource-control suite that the host this was run on cannot show, each as a limitation with its
# measured cause. Tab separated, one row per checks.tsv row of an environment ("<id>.<env>", host or hostv1 only):
#   id  class  accepts  cause  proof  requires  explanation
# A failing row becomes a LIMIT only when all three conditions hold (resctl-judge.py):
#   accepts  the value matches this specific pattern (the value resctl reported for the limitation, never any failure)
#   cause    every condition holds on the measured facts of any session: FACT~REGEX or FACT!~REGEX, joined by " && "
#   proof    every row named here is PASS and is the same fact in the cgroup v2 test bed guest, which shows that the
#            behaviour works wherever the cause does not apply
# A leaked value (the operation worked where it had to be refused) is never a limitation. Rows of the areas build,
# layout, isolation, terminate, recover and lifecycle cannot be limited: the kill domains and the system domain have no
# exception. `class` is one of host-hw host-kernel host-config (the classes of tools-test/limits.tsv).
# Four limits have one cause: the memory controller of this host is a cgroup v1 controller, so the unified hierarchy
# has no memory controller and the v2-only memory files (memory.low, memory.high, memory.oom.group) have nothing to bind
# to. resctl serves memory.max, the swap limit and the OOM kill through v1, and reports each v2-only setting as
# "unbound=<setting>: needs the cgroup v2 memory controller" instead of pretending to apply it.
# Two have another: root on this host lacks CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, so the kernel does not keep the OOM bias resctl gives a
# workload as that workload's minimum (it raises it all the same, and the supervisor raises it again when it is lowered),
# and resctl cannot lower the OOM score of a critical process to the preference of the policy (it says so instead).
system_protection.host
column3: ^unsupported:unbound=system memory\.low: needs the cgroup v2 memory controller$
column6: a cgroup v2 memory controller in the unified hierarchy (kernel parameter cgroup_no_v1=memory or cgroup_no_v1=all, or no v1 memory hierarchy mounted)
column7: memory.low, the protection of the system domain from reclaim, exists only in cgroup v2; this host serves memory through cgroup v1, so resctl cannot protect the system domain from memory reclaim here (the system domain is still outside every kill domain and has its own limits and CPU weight)

column3: ^unsupported:unbound=system memory\.low: needs the cgroup v2 memory controller$
column6: a cgroup v2 memory controller in the unified hierarchy (kernel parameter cgroup_no_v1=memory or cgroup_no_v1=all, or no v1 memory hierarchy mounted)
column7: the same limit as system_protection.host, with the v1 freezer as the lifecycle backend

column1: oom_group.host
column6: a cgroup v2 memory controller in the unified hierarchy (kernel parameter cgroup_no_v1=memory or cgroup_no_v1=all, or no v1 memory hierarchy mounted)
column7: memory.oom.group (an OOM kill takes the whole workload) exists only in cgroup v2; with cgroup v1 memory the kernel kills one process at a time, and resctl says so rather than claiming a whole-workload kill (a workload's kill domain still ends the rest on termination)

column1: memory_high.host
column6: a cgroup v2 memory controller in the unified hierarchy (kernel parameter cgroup_no_v1=memory or cgroup_no_v1=all, or no v1 memory hierarchy mounted)
column7: memory.high (throttle and reclaim before the hard limit) exists only in cgroup v2; with cgroup v1 memory a workload is held only by memory.max and killed at it, and resctl says so rather than pretending to throttle

column3: ^unsupported:CAP_SYS_RESOURCE is not in the capability set:
column6: CAP_SYS_RESOURCE for resctl (root without it, as in this sandbox or in containers that drop it, cannot make the kernel keep the bias)
column7: the bias toward the OOM killer is applied on this host too (oom_bias.host), but without CAP_SYS_RESOURCE the kernel does not keep it as the minimum of the workload, which can lower it again

column1: critical_oom.host
column3: ^unsupported:CAP_SYS_RESOURCE is not in the capability set: a registered critical process keeps its OOM score
column6: CAP_SYS_RESOURCE for resctl (root without it, as in this sandbox or in containers that drop it, cannot lower an OOM score)
column7: the registration of a critical process works on this host, but without CAP_SYS_RESOURCE the kernel refuses to lower its oom_score_adj to the preference of the policy; resctl warns, audits it and probe says oom.lower=no
